baseline.name: Calcite Substation Construction
baseline.description: Construct new Calcite 230 kV Substation to interconnect renewable generation projects.

date.label: Reported projected or actual in-service date

locationAssumptions: Published latitude/longitude is interpreted as decimal WGS84 for map display only; the source does not state its datum or positional accuracy.

proposal.name: Southern California Edison Company
proposal.scope: Planned Calcite substation equipment. Excludes the customer solar/storage facilities and customer-owned gen-tie portion.

evidence.finding: The county final EIR explicitly assigns intended future substation ownership to SCE.

evidence.locator: PDF/printed page 4, project overview; page 13, gen-tie extension
evidence.finding: The utility-authored description expands SCE to Southern California Edison Company and separates the customer-owned connection from the utility-side facilities.
The observed utility page describes the planned Calcite station at Lucerne Valley and a 2028–2029 construction horizon, consistent with the TPR project identity.

decisions.identityAssessment: Exact distinctive station name, Lucerne Valley setting and new renewable-interconnection purpose agree. No public crosswalk to native SP-01 or program 6902 was found; identity is a curated name/scope match, not an externally stated ID join.
limitations: Ownership language is prospective; it does not prove operating-asset title on June 1, 2026. The undated current webpage is an observation on September 30, not an edition as-of statement.
Public documents describe 220 kV while the TPR row records 230 kV. Preserve both source meanings without replacing the original voltage.

Earlier Stagecoach material and current Sienna material concern different generator customers. The proposal covers only the Calcite substation. The final EIR retains edit-marked connection counts; no quantity or footprint is inferred from flattened text.
decisions.missingInput: For a claim of present ownership, obtain an effective ownership/asset record for the built equipment. Coordinator must decide whether explicitly labeled planned ownership is acceptable in the revision contract.

baseline.description: This project involves conversion of the current bank-on-bus configuration to a bank on circuit breaker configuration for the Lugo 1AA & 2AA 500/220 kV transformer banks.

date.label: Reported projected or actual in-service date

notes: The source notes describe operational assets with remaining project work; the source row lifecycle is retained.

locationAssumptions: Published latitude/longitude is interpreted as decimal WGS84 for map display only; the source does not state its datum or positional accuracy.

evidence.locator: PDF page 44 / printed 42, PIN 6791, CWBS CETETTPRL679100
evidence.finding: The utility capital workpaper matches the TPR accounting/program alias and Lugo double-breaker work.

evidence.locator: PDF page 48 / printed 45, WBS CET-ET-TP-RL-679100 and table header
evidence.finding: The 100% field is headed % ISO; it is not an equipment-ownership percentage.

decisions.identityAssessment: Program 6791 and normalized CWBS match the row aliases; work-order 800308934 and explicit ownership of both 1AA/2AA bank conversion equipment remain uncorroborated.

May 2023 workpaper forecasts December 1, 2024 in-service; the June 2026 TPR reports June 29, 2032. No date replacement or completed-work inference is made.

baseline.name: Lugo-Victorville 500kV Transmission Line Upgrade  (Lugo-Victorville Thermal Overloads)
baseline.description: Thermal Overloads on Lugo - Victorville 500 kV Transmission Line during N-2 loss of either Eldorado – Lugo 500 kV with Eldorado –Mohave 500 kV

date.label: Reported projected or actual in-service date

locationAssumptions: Published latitude/longitude is interpreted as decimal WGS84 for map display only; the source does not state its datum or positional accuracy.
The displayed center is the arithmetic midpoint of the two published endpoints, not a surveyed route center or the complete work footprint.

evidence.finding: CAISO describes joint SCE/LADWP line ownership and separately owned upgrade portions; SCE work comprises four towers and Lugo terminal equipment.
The TPR program alias matches a Lugo breaker/disconnect capital item, which supports a narrower equipment association.

decisions.identityAssessment: Line endpoints, thermal-overload purpose and program 8029 support association, but the TPR work unit does not explicitly say SCE portion or delimit the complete row to those terminal assets.
limitations: The 2017 planning document is historical and includes an obsolete December 2018 forecast. The 2023 workpaper forecasts January 2025; neither replaces the TPR June 2027 date.
Neither the full line nor the endpoint midpoint may be treated as a wholly SCE-owned work footprint. A source-scoped single-owner label would still misrepresent unresolved joint scope.
decisions.missingInput: A dated crosswalk from SP-30 / program 8029 to the exact SCE-owned portion, plus current ownership boundary for included line and terminal equipment. Otherwise retain mixed ownership and no scalar owner.

baseline.name: Eldorado 220 kV Jointed-Owned Bus Split (Section A)
baseline.description: Split the Joint-Owned Eldorado 220 kV Bus and reconfigure the T/L configuration to lower the short circuit duty to maintain safety and reliability.

date.label: Reported projected or actual in-service date

locationAssumptions: Published latitude/longitude is interpreted as decimal WGS84 for map display only; the source does not state its datum or positional accuracy.

evidence.finding: CAISO identifies multiple bus co-owners and a sectionalizing/line-relocation scope. SCE is the submitter, not stated sole owner.

decisions.identityAssessment: The joint bus split, Eldorado site and short-circuit purpose match. TPR Section A and aliases 8545/CET-ET-TP-RL-854500 are retained; no external alias crosswalk or complete co-owner schedule was found.
limitations: The TPR title and description already identify joint ownership. Its title uses 220 kV, voltage field 230 kV, and CAISO uses 230 kV; do not normalize away the distinction.
The 2023 presentation is a recommended project scope, not a 2026 title/ownership schedule. Section A is not evidence that joint rights disappeared.
decisions.missingInput: Public ownership/participation schedule for the specific Section A bus, sectionalizing equipment and relocated terminals, including legal entities, shares/scope and effective date. Existing scalar-owner schema cannot honestly express an unresolved consortium.

baseline.name: Nevada Pacific DC Intertie Insulator Replacement
baseline.description: Replace approx. 80,000 old porcelain insulators pm ~432  miles of the PDCI with toughened glass insulators to support the planned  voltage upgrade

date.label: Reported projected or actual in-service date

notes: The source notes describe operational assets with remaining project work; the source row lifecycle is retained.
The source Notes column includes a construction-start clarification. No continuous construction interval is inferred.
The reported start belongs to a multi-year replacement program performed during scheduled outages, not continuous construction.

locationAssumptions: Published latitude/longitude is interpreted as decimal WGS84 for map display only; the source does not state its datum or positional accuracy.
The displayed center is the arithmetic midpoint of the two published endpoints, not a surveyed route center or the complete work footprint.

evidence.locator: PDF page 62 / printed 56, Pacific DC Intertie and Sylmar Converter Station
evidence.finding: LADWP states a 40% interest in the southern PDCI portion and distinguishes BPA ownership north of the Nevada–Oregon border; operational agency is also separate.
The parent accounting bucket concerns Sylmar converter capital; it does not assign title to the specific Nevada insulators.

decisions.identityAssessment: PDCI context is supported, but the 432-mile Nevada insulator work and work-order 901994846 are not tied to a specific ownership segment by the external evidence.
limitations: The TPR coordinates span the wider intertie while the description specifies a Nevada work segment. No geometry, segment boundary or owner is inferred from the midpoint.
A 2023 southern-system ownership percentage does not establish the current title of every replaced insulator, nor a sole SCE owner. LADWP operating-agent status is not a substitute.
decisions.missingInput: A public dated work-order/asset schedule connecting 901994846 and the 80,000-insulator scope to exact jointly or separately owned Nevada spans and legal owners.

baseline.name: Palo Verde - PL R9 (4 single phase reactors) replacement and adding new reactor switcher
baseline.description: Replace Palo Verde R9 reactor and add new reactor switcher

date.label: Reported projected or actual in-service date

locationAssumptions: Published latitude/longitude is interpreted as decimal WGS84 for map display only; the source does not state its datum or positional accuracy.

evidence.locator: PDF page 51 / printed 48, WBS CET-OT-OT-ME-465100 / PIN 4651
evidence.finding: The exact parent accounting bucket is Palo Verde switchrack capital. It supplies neither an R9 equipment match nor an ownership schedule.

decisions.identityAssessment: Accounting alias 4651 matches only the parent bucket. No external equipment-level crosswalk to work-order 904011808 / PL R9 and its four single-phase reactors or new switcher was found.
limitations: Palo Verde nuclear generating-station ownership and nearby transmission-line ownership cannot establish ownership of this switchrack reactor bank.
Capital allocation and % ISO classification do not establish legal title. The TPR reported December 31, 2026 date remains unchanged.
decisions.missingInput: Public equipment ownership/participation schedule for Palo Verde PL R9, its four single-phase reactors and new reactor switcher, cross-referenced to 904011808 and dated for the relevant planning scope.

applicationConstraints: Qualification is not approval to write runtime data.
A future revision must preview the proposed owner, its prospective/date qualifier and evidence; preserve all local notes and all unrelated fields.
Fingerprint is a strict baseline comparison aid, not permission to overwrite a changed record. Identity, edition and relevant fields must agree; local changes need explicit preservation/review.
No owner proposal changes geometry, unverified location confidence, lifecycle, source dates or calculation policy. No new eligible pair is claimed.
